key_insight: Polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation reveals hidden, opposite-handed chiral responses in a 2D halide perovskite, enabling strong telecom-band circularly polarized light detection with very large circular dichroism.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a path to compact telecom-wavelength chiral photodetectors and anti-counterfeiting or optical-encryption devices based on perovskite nonlinear optics.
method: Use the chiral 2D perovskite (R/S-MBACl)2PbI4 as the nonlinear optical medium.
Measure third-harmonic generation with polarization-resolved detection to separate orthogonal THG channels.
Compare circularly polarized light responses to quantify THG circular dichroism and dissymmetry.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exceptionally large dissymmetry factors exceeding 1.9 when hidden chiral contributions are separated, whereas conventional total-THG analysis underestimates the effect.
watch_item: Performance claims depend on polarization-resolved measurement; using only total THG intensity can mask the true chiral response and misrepresent device sensitivity.
paper_title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite
